meta.title: `Implement missing members` code action on `std::alloc::Allocator` gives parameter invalid name
meta.fix_ref: rust-lang/rust-analyzer#21665 (fix: prevent qualifying parameter names in add_missing_impl_members)
meta.build_notes: GitHub release assets rust-analyzer-aarch64-apple-darwin.gz of the weekly tags 2026-02-16 and 2026-02-23; git tag --contains puts the fix first in 2026-02-23. The sysroot is the local rustup toolchain (rustc 1.98.1). The generated signatures come from the Allocator trait of the local std (rustc 1.98.1); the reporter used rustc 1.95.0-nightly (2026-01-22). The pre build cannot load a Cargo workspace with the local cargo 1.98 (it passes --lockfile-path; attempt 1), so attempt 2 describes the crate with a rust-project.json.
meta.notes: The assist transforms the trait's method signatures into the impl's scope with a path transform that also rewrote identifier patterns: the parameter ptr resolves to the module std::ptr, so it was printed qualified ('std::ptr: std::ptr::NonNull<u8>'). A path pattern still parses, so the case uses the specification probe edit_text_differs; the expected text is the issue's generated code with the parameter name as the issue says it should be (ptr).

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the session keeps checkOnSave off (native analysis only).

files.note: verbatim with the cursor marker $0 removed from the impl body '{$0}'

a rust-project.json describing the single library crate (root module src/lib.rs, edition 2021, no dependencies); rust-analyzer discovers the sysroot itself ('discovering sysroot'); it replaces the Cargo.toml of attempt 1 because the pre build cannot load a Cargo workspace with the local cargo 1.98 (--lockfile-path)

repro.steps: Open src/lib.rs. With the cursor in the empty body of 'unsafe impl Allocator for Foo {}' (line 3, character 31, the issue's $0) apply 'Implement missing members'. Reported: deallocate's first parameter is named 'std::ptr'. Probe (specification): the edited src/lib.rs must equal the issue's generated code with that parameter named ptr (snippet placeholders stripped).

expected.source: issue body (the generated code shown, with the parameter name std::ptr replaced by ptr as the issue states)

attempts.summary: Cargo project (Cargo.toml scaffold): invalid. The pre build 2026-02-16 failed to load the workspace with the local cargo 1.98 ('cargo metadata ... unexpected argument --lockfile-path'), so std was not loaded, the Allocator trait was unresolved and no code action was offered ('offered: []'). The post build 2026-02-23 loaded it and produced exactly the expected text (3/3).
attempts.verdict: invalid (pre build cannot load the Cargo workspace)

expected.source: issue body (the generated code shown, with the parameter name std::ptr replaced by ptr as the issue states)

attempts.summary: Run 2026-09-23T11:3x (this case revision, rust-project.json): invalid on both builds ('offered: []'). The session logs show one indexed crate and no sysroot crates: without an explicit sysroot in rust-project.json these builds load no std, so std::alloc::Allocator is unresolved and 'Implement missing members' is not offered. The case needs std's Allocator; the only remaining setups are a machine-specific absolute sysroot path in rust-project.json or an older cargo toolchain, so the case stays not reproduced here (pre-check 4: the pre build 2026-02-16 does not load a Cargo workspace with cargo 1.98). The post build reproduced the issue's expected text exactly in attempt 1.
attempts.verdict: invalid (no std without an explicit sysroot)
